name: A fisherman, Napoule
bio: A fisherman at La Napoule, on the Riviera, to whom Wilde described himself as 'practically engaged' in a letter to Robert Ross of 2 January 1899. The letter calls him 'a fisherman of extraordinary beauty, age eighteen'. Nothing else about him - name, family, how they met, what became of it - appears in the pages read.
bio_note: Sole source: Wilde to Robert Ross, 2 January 1899, Napoule, Complete Letters (2000), p. 1116. He is distinct from the collective mentions on the same tier - 'The fishing population of the Riviera have the same freedom from morals as the Neapolitans have' (Ross, 27 December 1898, printed 1112) and the Napoule fisher-lads (printed c. 1119), which name no individual. Dates: none recorded. Frankel quotes the same sentence at printed p. 245 - 'I am practically engaged to a fisherman of extraordinary beauty, age eighteen' - and gives him no name and no dates either. No birth or death date is recorded, and none is likely to be found: the record preserves a first name (or a trade) in another man's correspondence and no surname to search by.
